basis: Cash net profit after tax from continuing operations for the full year ended 30 June 2026 versus the restated full year ended 30 June 2025. Movement evidence: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.26, "Cash net profit after tax ... increased $730 million or 7% ... to $10,982 million." Comparator evidence: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.27, "Net profit after tax from continuing operations – cash basis 10,982 10,252." CBA says the cash basis is used by management to present a clear view of operating results and is not cash accounting or cash flow (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.17, "It is not a measure based on cash accounting or cash flows."). Contributions are algebraic cash-basis P&L line movements: operating drivers are before tax and the full disclosed tax movement is shown separately, so no undisclosed after-tax allocation is assumed.

drivers.name: Net interest income
drivers.narrative: The largest positive driver. Net interest income rose to $25,586 million from $24,023 million. CBA attributes the increase mainly to a $92 billion increase in average interest earning assets, including $60 billion of lending-asset growth. Reported NIM fell 3 basis points to 2.05%, but CBA says underlying NIM was stable after excluding liquid-asset growth. Volume and margin are unquantified separately in dollars because CBA discloses only their combined $1,563 million NII effect.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.28, "Net interest income was $25,586 million, an increase of $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year."
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.28, "The result was driven by a $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.28, "net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year to 2.05%"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.28, "Excluding growth in liquid assets ... net interest margin was stable."
CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p.25, "Net interest income 1,563"

drivers.name: Other operating income
drivers.narrative: Other operating income increased to $4,638 million from $4,442 million. Higher insurance income, equities income and one-off gains were partly offset by lower Structured Asset Finance, foreign exchange, deposit-fee and credit-card-fee income. CBA does not quantify the dollar contribution of each subdriver, so those subdrivers are unquantified.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.30, "Other operating income was $4,638 million, an increase of $196 million or 4% on the prior year."
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.26, "primarily driven by higher insurance income and the benefit of one-off gains"
CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p.25, "Other operating income 196"

drivers.name: Inflation-related operating expenses
drivers.narrative: Inflation added $455 million to underlying operating expenses, reducing cash NPAT through the pre-tax P&L bridge. Wage inflation is specifically identified within staff costs.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Inflation 455"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Staff expenses increased by $288 million ... driven by wage inflation"

drivers.name: Investment in technology operating expenses
drivers.narrative: Technology investment added $444 million to underlying operating expenses. CBA identifies cloud volumes, software licensing, amortisation, vendor inflation, infrastructure, resilience and AI capabilities as important cost pressures.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Investment in technology 444"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Information technology services expenses increased by $393 million or 16%"

drivers.name: Investment in frontline and operations operating expenses
drivers.narrative: Additional investment in frontline and operations added $128 million to underlying operating expenses. CBA also cites higher staff costs in frontline and operations in its group commentary.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Investment in frontline and operations 128"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.26, "higher staff costs in frontline and operations"

drivers.name: Other underlying operating-expense factors
drivers.narrative: CBA's underlying-expense bridge assigns $96 million to other factors. The category is not further reconciled in dollars and is therefore not decomposed.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Other 96"

drivers.name: Productivity initiatives
drivers.narrative: Productivity initiatives offset $404 million of underlying expense growth, raising cash NPAT relative to a bridge without those savings. Together, inflation, technology, frontline and operations, other factors and productivity reconcile to the disclosed $719 million increase in underlying expenses.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Productivity (404)"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.31, "Underlying operating expenses were $13,585 million, an increase of $719 million"

drivers.name: Restructuring and notable items
drivers.narrative: Restructuring and notable-item expense rose to $170 million from $130 million, a $40 million negative movement. FY26 covered provisions for NZ legal proceedings, an additional goodwill payment following ASIC's Better Banking review and domestic remediation; FY25 covered domestic and NZ remediation and a Bankwest restructuring provision. CBA does not disclose a dollar split among the FY26 categories.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.27, "Restructuring and notable items ... (170) (130)"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.27, "FY26 relates to provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ"

drivers.name: Loan impairment expense
drivers.narrative: Loan impairment expense increased to $788 million from $726 million. Higher charges in Retail Banking Services and New Zealand more than offset lower charges in Business Banking and Institutional Banking and Markets. CBA cites portfolio growth, geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty and cost-of-living pressure.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.34, "Loan impairment expense was $788 million, an increase of $62 million or 9%"

CBA-FY26-asx-announcement.pdf, PDF p.2, "Loan impairment expense increased mainly reflecting portfolio growth, cost-of-living pressures"

drivers.name: Corporate tax expense
drivers.narrative: Corporate tax expense rose to $4,699 million from $4,491 million, reducing the year-on-year cash NPAT movement by $208 million. The effective cash tax rate nevertheless declined to 30.0% from 30.5% because non-deductible expenses decreased.

disagreements.issue: Continuing-operations versus including-discontinued-operations FY25 cash NPAT
disagreements.values: FY25 cash NPAT was $10,252 million from continuing operations and $10,253 million including discontinued operations.
disagreements.reason: The FY26 bank commentary and every operating line in the attribution are on a continuing-operations basis; discontinued operations contributed $1 million in FY25 and nil in FY26.

disagreements.values: The FY26 presentation reports cash NPAT of $11.0 billion and growth of 7.1%; the profit announcement reports $10,982 million and 7%.
disagreements.preferred: $10,982 million and $730 million movement; 7% as CBA's headline rounded growth rate.
disagreements.reason: The values are consistent after rounding; the profit announcement provides the exact dollar amount, while the presentation provides the more precise percentage.
citations: CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p.5, "Cash NPAT $11.0bn"
CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p.7, "10,252 10,982 ... +7.1%"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.26, "increased $730 million or 7% ... to $10,982 million"

disagreements.issue: FY25 divisional comparatives were restated in FY26
disagreements.values: FY25 document: Retail $5,395 million, Business $4,092 million, Institutional $1,224 million, New Zealand $1,198 million, Corporate Centre $(1,657) million. FY26 restated comparatives: $5,330 million, $4,092 million, $1,238 million, $1,195 million and $(1,603) million, respectively. Both sets sum to group continuing cash NPAT of $10,252 million.
disagreements.preferred: FY26 restated divisional comparatives for any current-period divisional comparison.
disagreements.reason: CBA explicitly says comparative information was restated to conform to current-period presentation. This attribution uses the unchanged group total, so the restatement does not alter the $730 million movement.
citations: CBA-FY25-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.16, "Cash net profit after tax, by division"
CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p.16, "Comparative information has been restated to conform with presentation in the current period."

limitations: CBA does not disclose dollar contributions for volume versus margin within the $1,563 million net-interest-income increase; those subdrivers remain unquantified.
CBA does not disclose dollar contributions for the individual causes within the $196 million other-operating-income increase.

The underlying-expense categories are management bridge categories rather than separately audited income-statement line items; the chart quantifies them, but the $96 million other category is not decomposed.

CBA does not publish after-tax contributions for each operating driver. The attribution therefore uses disclosed pre-tax P&L movements and the disclosed tax movement as a separate line; applying an assumed tax rate to each driver would be unsupported.
Confidence ratings are analyst probabilities of agreement with CBA's own disclosure, not figures reported by CBA.
